issues.legal_issue: Income received from shops held under an arrangement in which possession was transferred in return for an advance and shop receipts were to liquidate the advance was not rental income assessable as a revenue receipt.
material_facts: The assessment included receipts from shops on land belonging to others as rental income.
Under agreements, the assessee or his sons paid advances and obtained possession of shops, with the right to use them or let them out.
The agreements provided for the shops to remain in their possession for fixed periods, and the receipts from them were to be appropriated towards liquidation of the advances.
The agreements provided for possession to revert to the owners after the agreed periods.
issues.conclusion: The transactions were mortgages, not leases, and the receipts were not revenue receipts assessable to income tax; the High Court's decision in favour of the assessee was affirmed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 58(d) of the Transfer of Property Act, a usufructuary mortgage involves possession of mortgaged property being delivered or promised to the mortgagee, who may retain it and appropriate rents and profits towards interest or mortgage money. A fixed term calculated in advance as sufficient to liquidate the debt does not by itself change the transaction's character. Section 105 defines a lease as a transfer of a right to enjoy property for consideration such as a price or rent. The Court applied Ishan Chandra v. Sujan Bibi, Tukaram Bin Mairal v. Ramchand Malukchand, and Mahmad Muse Umarji v. Bagas Amanji Umar, and distinguished Nidha Sah v. Murlidhar, where there was no liquidation of a debt through rents and profits.

predicates.income_tax_assessment_disputes_rental_re: A tax assessment dispute concerns whether receipts from property are taxable as rental income.
predicates.possession_transferred_for_advance: An owner transfers possession of property to another person in return for an advance.
predicates.receipts_appropriated_to_liquidate_debt: The arrangement provides that receipts or profits from the property will be applied to liquidate the advance.
predicates.receipts_are_not_taxable_as_revenue_inco: The receipts are not assessable as revenue income.

issues.definition: When a tax assessment dispute concerns rental receipts and possession was transferred for an advance whose liquidation was to come from the property receipts, those receipts are not taxable as revenue income.
